title: Let add opt out of pass inheritance
lead: `slicer add --pass ''` still files the item under the previous item's pass, so the only way to add an item with no pass after a passed tail is `add` then `set ID --pass ''`.
findings_note: S127 docs audit: add --pass '' still inherits the previous item's pass

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: `ops.add` computes `pass_key` as `fields.get("pass_key") or <previous item's pass>` (`src/slicer/ops.py:105`), so an explicit empty string is treated as omitted. Verified in a scratch project: after `add a --pass v1`, `add b --pass '' --json` returned `"pass": "v1"`. `set --pass ''` does clear a pass, so the two commands disagree about what `--pass ''` means.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ops.py` (`add`), `src/slicer/cli.py` (`add --pass` help)
- `docs/getting-started.md` §7, which documents the `set` workaround
- tests for `add`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `add TITLE --pass ''` after a passed tail files the item with no pass.
2. `add TITLE` with `--pass` omitted still inherits, as documented.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Distinguish an omitted `--pass` (None) from an explicit empty one in `add`, and update the help and §7.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The tests above pass; the suite and `slicer check` pass.
